summary: A Yes vote amends the existing voter-approval requirement so the City Council can approve zoning changes to single-family residential areas without a neighborhood voter approval vote.

housing.text: The League of Women Voters supports Measure O because it removes a neighborhood-level veto over R-1 zoning changes and allows the City Council to consider them through the normal public process.
housing.quote: Measure O removes precisely the sort of neighborhood-level veto that this position identifies as a housing constraint.

housing.text: A no vote would retain the Measure D requirement for majority approval from residents in an affected neighborhood before certain single-family zoning changes.
housing.quote: A yes vote on Measure O would give the Albany City Council greater authority over zoning in single-family residential areas and reduce the direct approval power granted to neighborhood voters under Measure D.
